messages:
marie: Quick heads-up: I opened a small PR to reconcile audit export docs with the runtime change and add a compact field-level redaction example — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/634
jon: reading now. avoid phrases like "permanent" or "forever". suggest: "Audit artifacts are retained per-account according to configured retention settings and applicable legal holds." Also add contact path for legal-hold requests.
m21 (marie): updated wording to: "Audit artifacts are retained per-account according to configured retention settings and applicable legal holds. For legal-hold requests, contact support@redwood.ai and your account rep." @jon OK?
jon: looks good. explicitly state that legal holds override retention TTLs and request headers. add sample TTL values (e.g., 90d, 365d).
eli: small security note: the export examples show raw identifiers. include a compact example for client-side redaction and one line on export encryption/integrity (KMS + bundle hash). keep it short.
siva: small JS redaction snippet to drop into the PR (feel free to shorten):
```
// client-side field-level redaction before write
const stream = await client.audit.export({query: 'since:2025-01-01'});
for await (const row of stream) {
  delete row.user_email;
  row.user_id = hash(row.user_id);
  writeRedacted(row);
}
```
siva: also callout: runtime route changed in last deploy from `/v1/audit/records` -> `/v1/audit/logs`. update snippets.
marie: thanks — updated both snippets and the curl examples. I added a backcompat note: runtime accepts `/v1/audit/records` as a legacy path through 2026-09-30.
docs-bot: PR 634 opened by marie — reviewers requested: jon, eli, siva.
marie: adding TTL header examples per @jon:
```
# header-based retention examples
X-Redwood-Retention: 90d
X-Redwood-Retention: 365d
```
marie: combined export + redaction quick example for QA:
```
# export to file with TTL header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Retention: 90d" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/logs/export -o audit.ndjson

# one-liner mask with python
python -c "import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  r=json.loads(l)
  r.pop('user_email',None)
  print(json.dumps(r))" < audit.ndjson > audit.masked.ndjson
```
jon: replace the word "mask" with "field-level redaction" for legal precision. also add a sentence that retention headers are account-level directives and may be constrained by org policy.
marie: applied both edits: replaced wording, added: "Retention headers are account-level directives; organization admins may enforce stricter minimums via account policy."
eli: adding the short encryption/integrity line: "Exports are encrypted using customer-managed or Redwood-managed KMS; exported bundles include a SHA-256 integrity checksum for verification. Customers with HSM requirements should contact security for private deployment options."
marie: added that sentence. CI linkcheck initially failed due to an old internal link to `/docs/audit-schema` — fixed to `/docs/reference/audit-schema.md`.
qa: can we get a tiny runbook snippet for support to reproduce an export + redaction flow? a curl + python chain is ideal.
marie: added the curl+python chain above as requested. kept it intentionally tiny for support reproduction.
siva: pushed the updated JS snippet and removed any example implying storage of SSNs.
jon: final legal pass, LGTM. one tiny phrasing swap: "suspend automated deletion" -> "override automated deletion".
marie: applied phrasing swap, CI is green now. merging once three approvals are in.
ci-bot: docs build: linkcheck OK, lint OK, preview: https://deploy-preview-634--docs.redwood.ai/audit-export-guide
marie: post-merge note: will follow up with a micro-PR to add an internal ops playbook link for legal-hold handling (internal only).
eli: please ping security before expanding the KMS/HSM wording for enterprise customers.
marie: will do. release note drafted: "docs: update audit export guidance, add field-level redaction examples, retention header samples, and KMS/integrity note" :white_check_mark:
qa: thanks — this made support reproduction much faster.
